ToolCall (agent/core/tool/models.py:20-23) has id: str. query_database.py:227-263 uses exactly these (call.id, block.get('type')/block.get('id'), message.role, following.tool_call_id), guarding the Optional fields with `or ()`. llm.py:158-167 _build_payload: for role=='assistant' with provider_content not None, it deep-copies provider_content and appends it as the assistant message content, never consulting tool_calls. Only thinking/redacted_thinking blocks are filtered (older turns), so tool_use blocks are kept; the branch continues before the tool_calls serialization path. Claim holds even with empty tool_calls. The rejection line concerns truncate_messages, unrelated.

query_database.py:243-263 (_first_unanswered_tool_use) collects ids from the assistant message, then walks messages[index+1:] collecting tool_call_id from consecutive role=='tool' messages, breaking at the first non-tool message; unanswered if ids not subset of answered. anthropic/llm.py:169-190 (_build_payload) groups consecutive role=='tool' messages directly into a single user message of tool_result blocks keyed by tool_call_id. This matches the claim: a tool_use is answered only by tool messages in the run directly after the assistant message. Absolute-claim trace: an assistant tool_use followed by an intervening user/assistant message then a tool message. The checker breaks at the intervening message, so it is unanswered, matching the API rule. Minor edge: the builder drops tool messages with falsy tool_call_id (llm.py:174), while the checker treats a None id as answerable by a None tool message (query_database.py:238-239,260). This needs a tool_use block with no id, which the API would reject anyway, and no shipped producer is shown creating one, so it does not break the claim. The rejection line about truncate_messages return values is unrelated to this claim.

Read query_database.py:266-356 in head view. get_conversation is in try/except Exception (284-294); the scan _first_unanswered_tool_use is in try/except Exception (297-305); getattr(store, 'truncate_messages', None) with a None check logs ERROR (309-319); the truncate call is guarded for ConversationOwnerMismatchError and Exception, each logged at ERROR (320-340); falsy return logs ERROR (341-350), matching the rejection line (truncate_messages -> bool). Unguarded statements: line 283 agent.conversation_store (documented as always set by Agent.__init__ at 369-371), line 308 len(conversation.messages) - cut, getattr at 309, and the truthiness test at 341. Tried the hint's counterexamples: Conversation.messages is declared List[Message] (agent/core/storage/models.py:36), and the same list was already iterated successfully at 298, so len() cannot raise for any shipped store. getattr on shipped stores (BoundedConversationStore, MemoryConversationStore) is a plain method lookup, and truncate_messages returns a bool, so no shipped caller produces a raising property or a raising __bool__. cut is an int or None, so the subtraction is safe. Property holds for all producible inputs. The wording 'each guarded' is slightly loose, since len and getattr are not in try blocks, but they are infallible on the typed inputs.

query_database.py:243-263 _first_unanswered_tool_use iterates range(start, len(messages)) and only returns an index in that range, so cut >= start always; _trim_unanswered_tool_use (298-321) truncates only at that cut, so nothing below the baseline index is removed. _conversation_baseline (208-224) reads len(messages) after the turn lock is held, before the agent run, so start is the length of the earlier history. Absolute-claim trace: a store whose conversation shrank or was replaced between baseline and trim (e.g. LRU eviction and recreation) makes start exceed or misalign with len(messages); the scan then covers fewer messages (empty range if start >= len) and cut still cannot fall below start, so no index below start is cut. A grep of src found no compaction or message-replacing code path in shipped code (agent.py only creates new empty conversations at 307/439); the per-conversation turn lock serializes calls. Only a hypothetical external writer that replaces earlier history with different content of equal or greater length could misalign start, which no shipped caller produces. The rejection line about truncate_messages returning None is unrelated to this claim.

conversation_store.py:98-143: truncate_messages is a plain `def` (synchronous), signature (conversation_id, user_id, length) -> bool; returns True after `del conversation.messages[length:]` (line 139-143), False for unknown id or length >= len; raises ConversationOwnerMismatchError when conversation.user.id != user_id (135-136). Also raises ValueError on negative length, which is an extra not contradicting the claim. Rejection line (declares -> bool at 98-122) confirmed by head bytes.

query_database.py:308 computes removed = len(conversation.messages) - cut from the Conversation returned by store.get_conversation; the WARNING at 351-356 logs conversation_id and removed. The module docstring (tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:4) states without qualification that a stopped query_database call never leaves an unanswered tool_use. src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:266-345 _trim_unanswered_tool_use has failure branches that deliberately leave it in place and only log ERROR. A store without truncate_messages hits the early return at 310-319 (log text: 'left an unanswered tool_use that was not removed ... has no truncate_messages'). ConversationOwnerMismatchError (322-330) and any other Exception from truncate (331+) are logged and the function returns, as do get_conversation raising (286-294) and a scan error (299-305). The function's own docstring says the cleanup 'Never raises' and logs rather than removes. The file's own parametrized test, per the verify_hint, asserts the tool_use stays in those cases. The default BoundedConversationStore has truncate_messages, so the default path is covered, but embedder-supplied stores are a documented input (the code comments at 596-604 name embedder-supplied conversation_store). The claim therefore overstates the guarantee: it holds only for stores that implement truncate_messages and do not raise. The rejection about a None return from truncate_messages concerns a different defect (the falsy-return check) and does not cover this item. Impact is a wording overstatement in a test docstring.

Criteria file read: well-formed, criterion 1 matches this claim verbatim; judged with siblings. Code: query_database.py:593-612 takes the turn lock then reads baseline (user, message count) via _conversation_baseline (208-224). 633-644: `except asyncio.CancelledError` wraps agent.send_message and, when baseline_user and queued_id are set, calls _rollback_conversation(agent, queued_id, baseline_user.id, baseline_messages) then re-raises (no result). _rollback_conversation (359-442) is synchronous and calls BoundedConversationStore.truncate_messages (conversation_store.py:98-138), which drops messages past length, mutating the same Conversation the agent appended to. Result: C has exactly its pre-call messages. The next call then sees a history with no dangling tool_use. Test test_cancel_between_tool_use_and_tool_result_restores_history (tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:216-233) uses the real Agent, AnthropicLlmService with a recording stub client and BoundedConversationStore. It seeds a completed round, parks run_sql, and asserts the last stored message is the assistant tool_use. It then cancels, asserts the history equals `before`, and checks the next call returns 'Done.' and that its request payload has every tool_use followed by a tool_result with the same id (_assert_every_tool_use_answered, 179-194). Split conditions/alternatives: (a) conversation_id None -> queued_id None -> no rollback: outside the trigger (the claim is about a call on conversation C; the agent mints a private id no later call can name). (b) baseline read raising -> RuntimeError before the agent runs, nothing saved: outside the trigger (fails closed). (c) store without truncate_messages / raising / owner mismatch (rollback branches 384-426) -> logs ERROR and keeps history: outside the trigger (claim fixes a BoundedConversationStore; mismatch unreachable with _StaticUserResolver; fails closed with ERROR log). (d) cancellation while waiting for the lock (196-199): nothing saved, outside the trigger. (e) cancellation inside the post-run trim await: still caught by the same CancelledError clause and rolled back to baseline, which satisfies the outcome. (f) conversation evicted mid-call: truncate returns False, nothing to restore, outside the trigger.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text}; criterion 2 is this claim, so it counts. Traced src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py at head. _tool_use_ids (227-240) collects ids from message.tool_calls and from tool_use blocks in provider_content. _first_unanswered_tool_use (243-263) scans from the call's baseline `start`, over assistant messages only. It collects tool_call_ids from the run of role=tool messages directly after the assistant message, and returns the earliest index where ids is not a subset of answered. _trim_unanswered_tool_use (266-356) calls store.truncate_messages(conversation_id, user.id, cut). That drops everything from `cut` on, so earlier messages stay, including the call's user message (the user message precedes the assistant message, so cut >= its index+1). The trim is called on both the normal-return path (629-632) and the Exception path before re-raise (623-628), inside the turn lock, so the next call on C sees a history with no unanswered tool_use. Once the history is trimmed, the vendored builder gets no unmatched tool_use. I did not run the tests.

Code conditions split: `queued_id is None` (no conversation id), the baseline-user guard, store get_conversation raising, conversation None, scan raising, cut None, missing truncate_messages, truncate raising, ConversationOwnerMismatchError, and truncate returning False. Alternatives: queued_id None -> outside the trigger, since the claim is about a call on conversation C; conversation None or cut None -> outside the trigger, since there is no unanswered tool_use to trim; store/scan/truncate faults, no truncate_messages, owner mismatch and truncate returning False -> sibling criterion 5: 'logs at ERROR naming the store class, leaves the history as it was, and returns or raises the same result'. Those paths log at ERROR and return without replacing the call's result. The cancelled path -> outside the trigger (criterion 1 'cancelled'). No departure inside the trigger.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text}; criterion 4 matches this claim; judged as limited by the others. Call site src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:614-632: on a non-cancelled end (normal or Exception) _trim_unanswered_tool_use runs; the cancel path (633-644) is separate. In _trim_unanswered_tool_use (266-356) the only state-changing action is truncate_messages(cut) at 321, reached only after `if cut is None: return` (306-307) is passed; cut comes from _first_unanswered_tool_use(messages, start) (243-263), which returns None when every assistant message from this call's baseline has all tool_use ids (tool_calls and provider_content) answered by the directly following tool messages. So a call with no unanswered tool_use leaves history untouched, including a failed call's user message. Code condition split: (a) store.get_conversation raises -> logged at ERROR, return, history untouched: outside the trigger (fault, fails closed, history as appended anyway); (b) conversation is None -> return, nothing to trim: outside the trigger (no history); (c) scan raises -> logged, return, untouched: fault, fails closed; (d) cut is None -> return: the claimed outcome; (e) no truncate_messages / truncate raises / removed nothing -> only reached when cut is not None, i.e. an unanswered tool_use was saved: outside the trigger (needs saved unanswered tool_use); (f) baseline_user None or queued_id None (line 624/629) -> no trim, history untouched: matches claim. Test tests/unit/test_query_database_queue.py:240-266 (test_second_call_starts_after_first_fails) asserts messages == ['fails','second'] after a failed first call, with comment 'A failed call is not rolled back, so its message stays ahead of the next.'

Criterion 5 counts (criteria.json is a valid list with criterion 5 matching this claim). In _trim_unanswered_tool_use (src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:266-356), alternatives split: (a) get_conversation raises (285-294) -> ERROR via logger.exception naming type(store).__name__, returns: conforms. (b) no truncate_messages (309-319) -> logger.error naming the store class, returns: conforms. (c) truncate_messages raises generic Exception (331-340) -> logger.exception naming the store class: conforms. (d) truncate_messages raises ConversationOwnerMismatchError (322-330) -> logger.error WITHOUT type(store).__name__ (message only has the conversation id): departure from 'logs at ERROR naming the store class'. This is a store fault inside the trigger (truncate_messages raising) and no sibling criterion names it. (e) scanning stored messages raises (297-305) -> ERROR without store class either; arguably outside the literal 'reading the conversation' wording but also a silent-departure fault. History is left unchanged and the function returns without raising in all branches, so the 'same result' part holds; only the store-class naming fails for (d) (and (e)). The comment at 322-330 does not justify the omission.
